searchText: I'm starting to wonder if we even need the `payload_withheld` field. We could just use an empty payload to indicate it is withheld. Even with `payload_withheld`, you would still need to check if the payload is empty. It seems cleaner to eliminate an unnecessary field. You need to check for emptiness, if we go with SSZ optional then it's fine to remove the field. But we haven't committed yet to the Payload being a stable container Agree. SSZ optional is the cleanest. But for now why can't one say - If the payload is empty, then it's withheld - Else verify the payload I don't like to have to define the notion of "payload being empty" I read <@363800010518822915>'s article about delayed execution: https://ethresear.ch/t/advantage-of-pipelining-consensus-and-execution-delayed-execution/19668. From the EL dev perspective, it sounds very interesting. ELs will have much more time to attest correctly. Do all the currently considered ePBS designs provide more time for ELs? AFAIK there's only one ePBS design being considered so yes 🙂 honestly the only variant I am aware of that has a spec is Slot auctions which is a minor change from this one and that also has the same feature more abstractly, any version that doesn't rely on aggregated voting, but has a small committee to attest for the timeliness of the payload (what we are calling a PTC), will have this same feature (or rather *can* have the same feature) That's a fair point. We'll likely have to use ssz optional anyway right, only reason I haven't gone this route yet is that we don't have it 🙂 and I would want to have a working PoC and even an interop soon I believe we can achieve this in 2 months of hard work. Prysm already has a good start, but we haven't started on fork choice yet, which is the hardest part. Once the EIP is out, we'll need to redo previous PRs, such as removing the inclusion list. already working on that Which part? I don't want to be doign the samething as you. Actually we should bring this to internal channel since it's prysm specific.

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: I'm starting to wonder if we even need the `payload_withheld` field. We could just use an empty payload to indicate it is withheld. Even with `payload_withheld`, you would still need to check if the payload is empty. It seems cleaner to eliminate an unnecessary field.

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: You need to check for emptiness, if we go with SSZ optional then it's fine to remove the field. But we haven't committed yet to the Payload being a stable container

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content:
Agree. SSZ optional is the cleanest. But for now why can't one say
- If the payload is empty, then it's withheld
- Else verify the payload

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: I don't like to have to define the notion of "payload being empty"

excerpts.author: marekm3498
excerpts.content:
I read <@363800010518822915>'s article about delayed execution: https://ethresear.ch/t/advantage-of-pipelining-consensus-and-execution-delayed-execution/19668.

From the EL dev perspective, it sounds very interesting. ELs will have much more time to attest correctly. Do all the currently considered ePBS designs provide more time for ELs?

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: AFAIK there's only one ePBS design being considered so yes 🙂

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: honestly the only variant I am aware of that has a spec is Slot auctions which is a minor change from this one and that also has the same feature

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: more abstractly, any version that doesn't rely on aggregated voting, but has a small committee to attest for the timeliness of the payload (what we are calling a PTC), will have this same feature (or rather *can* have the same feature)

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: That's a fair point. We'll likely have to use ssz optional anyway

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: right, only reason I haven't gone this route yet is that we don't have it 🙂 and I would want to have a working PoC and even an interop soon
